headline: Exploited vCenter and Cisco Expressway flaws are due for patching by 23 November
plain_summary: Two widely used server products, VMware vCenter and Cisco Expressway, have flaws that are being exploited, and both are on CISA's list with a 23 November deadline. Separately, serious NGINX and PHP flaws have fixes available; no exploitation of the NGINX flaws has been confirmed. A large Japanese customer-data leak at a marketing vendor affects several companies. Anyone running these products should patch.

items.title: VMware vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 exploited by suspected state actor
items.why: Google says ARMORY CASTLE has exploited this authentication bypass since early September; CISA's deadline is 23 November.
items.action: Apply Broadcom's fixed vCenter builds (8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 or 9.1.1.0200) now; vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. Restrict inbound access to and egress from vCenter, following the hardening advice in Google's post.

items.title: Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC
items.why: A critical (CVSS 9.8) unauthenticated root command flaw was used against internet-exposed devices, and CISA lists it with a 23 November deadline.
items.action: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; Cisco says no workaround). If you cannot patch at once, F6 advises blocking TCP 4371-4372 except from trusted cluster node IPs.

items.title: NGINX flaws allow remote code execution over HTTP/2; public PoC exists
items.why: CERT-FR warns of unauthenticated code execution; Palo Alto Networks says it knows of no malicious exploitation.
items.action: Check every NGINX server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions (1.30.7 or 1.31.9) from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928, or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

items.title: PHP security releases fix 17 vulnerabilities, several rated critical
items.why: Reports say the critical issues need non-default or uncommon configurations, so default installs are not described as affected.
items.action: Update PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 and check for the non-default configurations the advisories describe.

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack on its applications
items.why: The Commission says a campaign detected 22 October took several applications offline; most are restored and no staff-wide data breach has been detected.
items.action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.

items.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million customers' data leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
items.why: ZOZO confirmed the leak at a marketing platform vendor; passwords are not held there and card data is not confirmed leaked.
items.action: ZOZO customers: be wary of phishing emails, texts or calls impersonating ZOZO, and do not open their links or attachments, as ZOZO advises.

items.title: Proximus mobile disruption: software bug, cyberattack ruled out
items.why: Proximus says an update the night before caused call and SMS problems on 20 November and rules out a cyberattack.
